audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings cross a known Colstrip perimeter break
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $54m annual base-rate increase for higher power-supply costs offset by $43m of removed Colstrip cost recovery; first-half 2026 net-income impact was filed as immaterial; owner-earnings impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor includes pre-transfer generation, operating costs and depreciation, while forecast OE reflects replacement power, revised rates, retained transmission and regulatory amortizations after the January 1, 2026 transfer.
audit_findings.evidence: Effective January 1, 2026, the Company transferred its ownership to NorthWestern.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter break is demonstrated, but its valuation materiality is unresolved. The latest filing says the transfer's first-half net-income effect was immaterial because several revenue and expense changes offset; that does not establish that cash owner earnings were unaffected. The omitted perimeter adjustment could raise or lower OE depending on replacement costs, regulatory recovery and retained transmission economics.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE line by line to a post-transfer pro forma, including removed Colstrip revenue and costs, replacement power, retained transmission and regulatory amortizations, then rerun all scenarios if pro forma OE differs materially.

audit_findings.title: Retained Colstrip liabilities may be an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $17m ARO and $34m Colstrip regulatory assets at June 30, 2026, plus $14m of posted surety support; joint-and-several excess exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any remediation cash cost not recovered through rates must reduce future OE or be deducted as a claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: While the obligations and liabilities with respect to Colstrip have been shared among the co-owners on a pro-rata basis, many of the environmental liabilities are joint and several under the law, so that if any co-owner failed to pay its share of such liability, the other co-owners (or any one of them) could be required to pay the defaulting co-owner‘s share (or the entire liability).
audit_findings.explanation: Retention of the remediation obligations and joint-and-several exposure is demonstrated, but an omitted common-equity claim is not. The recorded $17m ARO alone is about 0.8% of the $2,197m base equity value, or about $0.20 per share, and is accompanied by $34m of Colstrip regulatory assets. The potentially important issue is therefore unrecoverable cost or liability beyond the recorded amount, which the record does not quantify.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $17m ARO, $34m regulatory assets, expected cash-payment schedule and commission recovery orders; separately stress any unrecoverable amount and co-owner-default exposure, without treating the $14m surety as an additional liability unless drawn.

audit_findings.title: Known 2026 industrial-load loss is absent from the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $9m expected 2026 net-income decrease, equal to 6.2% of the $144.3m anchor; if it translates dollar-for-dollar to OE, current base-case scaling implies about $126m or $1.49 per share of value
audit_findings.mechanism: The known customer departure reduces recurring OE before scenario growth is applied.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income is expected to decrease $9 million compared to if we had served their load through December 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The load departure and $9m 2026 earnings step-down are demonstrated. The exact recurring OE loss remains unresolved because avoided supply costs, retained transmission revenue and rate mitigation have not been reconciled. Its filed scale is large enough to change the per-share valuation and buy-below level, even though it would not reverse the present conclusion that market price exceeds all scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Calculate the annualized after-cost OE loss from the April 2026 departure, including retained transmission and regulatory mitigation, adjust the starting OE before growth and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require dilution beyond the supplied share ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed expectation of up to $90m of 2026 common-stock issuance, of which $58m was issued through June 30, leaving up to $32m; at $37.55 this equals about 0.85m shares or 1.0% of 84.562703m, mechanically reducing base value by about $0.27 per share if proceeds add no incremental value; recurring dilution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional issuance increases the per-share denominator and assigns part of growth financed by new shareholders away from current holders.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2026, we expect to issue up to $230 million of long-term debt and up to $90 million of common stock to fund planned capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: This is primarily forward-looking because the supplied share count exceeds the July 24 outstanding count but does not establish issuances after that date or the recurring equity needed beyond 2026. The remaining announced 2026 amount is modest on its own, while the longer-term dilution associated with the capital program could be more important but is unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Verify shares issued after July 24, update fully diluted shares, and model annual equity funding alongside the capital expenditures and incremental OE supporting each growth case.

audit_findings.title: Separately added investment stakes may still affect the OE numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Bridge adds $145m of stakes; filed 2025 investment losses were $12m and the other non-reportable segment loss was $14m. The $12m loss equals 8.3% of anchor OE and, if retained in OE, corresponds to about $169m or $2.00 per share under current base-case scaling
audit_findings.mechanism: Investment gains, losses, expenses or distributions in OE duplicate or offset economics assigned separately to the $145m asset bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Realized and unrealized gains or losses in equity investments are included in net income.
audit_findings.explanation: The investments' effect on consolidated income is demonstrated, but whether those items survived the OE construction is unresolved. Retaining the 2025 losses would understate operating value while separately adding the stakes; retaining future gains would overstate it. The filed amounts are large enough to change valuation materially, so the numerator and bridge must be placed on a consistent claim basis.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $12m investment losses, related subsidiary expenses, distributions and cash-flow adjustments through the $144.3m anchor; remove all stake-related economics from OE or remove the separate $145m bridge value, then rerun consistently.

audit_findings.title: Noncash equity AFUDC may have been capitalized as current owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $11m of 2025 equity-related AFUDC, equal to 7.6% of the $144.3m anchor; if fully retained in OE, current base-case scaling implies about $155m or $1.83 per share of value
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity AFUDC increases accounting income before cash collection and therefore overstates current OE if not removed from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash inflow related to AFUDC does not occur until the related utility plant is placed in service and included in rate base.
audit_findings.explanation: The $11m noncash AFUDC recognition is demonstrated; its inclusion in the valuation numerator is only a possibility because the anchor calculation has not been traced. If included, its scale is material. Later rate recovery should enter OE only when collected, so the correction must avoid deducting the same economics twice.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $11m cash-flow add-back and any above-FERC AFUDC accrual to the OE worksheet, remove amounts included as current earnings, and rerun while preserving later cash recovery when it enters customer rates.
